_about: Field terms for F508, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

bits-per-letter.definition: the average number of binary digits needed to write down each letter of a text under a given model of the text; one bit halves the number of equally likely choices, so 4.75 bits per letter is the cost of picking blindly among 27 symbols
bits-per-letter.excludes: a count of bytes in a file, and any statement about meaning

n-gram-entropy.definition: the uncertainty of the next letter when the N minus 1 letters before it are known, averaged over the text; Shannon wrote it F with a subscript N, so F1 uses single-letter counts, F2 one letter of context and F3 two
n-gram-entropy.excludes: the entropy of the language as a whole, which is the limit as N grows

plug-in.definition: an entropy computed by putting the observed relative frequencies of a sample straight into the entropy formula, with no correction for the size of the sample
plug-in.excludes: corrected estimators that add a term for unseen or rare events

context-model.field: data compression and statistical language modelling
context-model.definition: a model that predicts the next symbol from counts of what followed the same few preceding symbols in training text, blending long and short contexts; prediction by partial matching (PPM) is the classic form
context-model.excludes: models that use word meaning, grammar or knowledge outside the letter counts

log-loss.field: information theory and machine learning; also called cross-entropy
log-loss.definition: the average of minus the base-2 logarithm of the probability a model gave to the letter that came next, in bits per letter; it is the length of the code an ideal coder driven by the model would write
log-loss.excludes: the share of letters guessed right, and the entropy of the text itself, which log loss can only bound from above

held-out.definition: text kept apart from the text a model was trained on and used only to score it
held-out.excludes: any text whose counts entered the model

guessing-game.definition: a reader guesses the next letter in order of preference until right; the share of letters found at the first, second and later guesses gives an upper and a lower bound on the entropy
guessing-game.excludes: a direct measure of the probabilities a reader holds

markov-chain.definition: a random text in which each symbol depends only on the two symbols before it, through a fixed table of probabilities, so its entropy per symbol can be computed exactly
markov-chain.excludes: real text, whose dependence reaches further back

zipf.definition: the observation that the frequency of a word falls roughly in inverse proportion to its rank in the frequency list
zipf.excludes: an exact law that holds for every word or every text

penalty.field: our usage, from machine learning practice on domain shift
penalty.definition: the extra log loss a reader pays on another kind of text compared with a reader trained on that kind of text, both scored on the same held-out passage
penalty.excludes: the difference in difficulty between two texts read by their own readers
